title: Job design
log: 2026-10-29T12:22:32Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: No point in the bank covers job design; the closest ones, the scientific and behavioural approaches, deal with management theories rather than how to design jobs for variety and responsibility.

draft.title: Job design
card: Job design is how a business arranges the tasks, duties and responsibilities in a role. A well designed job can keep workers engaged and interested in their work.
a job made up of a narrow set of tasks, repeated often. It can build speed and skill, but workers may become bored.
a job made up of a wide range of tasks. It gives workers more variety, but they may take longer to master each task.
A business can add variety by letting workers move between different tasks. It can add responsibility by giving workers more say over how and when they do their work.
draft.remember: Job design shapes the mix of tasks, variety and responsibility in a role, which affects how engaged workers are.

a.q: Which job is designed with specific tasks?
opts: A packer who only seals boxes all shift
A cook who preps, serves and cleans in turn
A clerk who handles sales, orders and complaints
A farmhand who moves between planting and repairs
a.why: Sealing boxes all shift is a narrow set of tasks repeated often, which is a specific job. The cook does three kinds of work in turn, so that job is designed with general tasks, not specific ones.
a.clue: Which role has the narrowest set of tasks?

b.q: Dev packs parcels at a Perth warehouse and says he is bored by doing one task all day. The manager lets staff rotate between packing, labelling and checking stock. Which job design change is this?
opts: Adding variety by widening the tasks in the job
Adding responsibility by giving staff control of the work
Making the job more specific to build speed
Reducing the number of tasks to lower boredom
b.why: Rotating between three tasks widens the mix of work, so it adds variety. It does not give staff more say over how or when they work, so it is not extra responsibility.
b.clue: Did staff gain more say, or more different tasks?

a.best: A packer who only seals boxes all shift

b.best: Adding variety by widening the tasks in the job
